messages:
priya: Heads up — we got a 3x spike in 5xxs for ap-southeast right after the Route53 failover at ~21:02 UTC. Latency steering routed a chunk to us-west and the NAT ports there blew up.

nate: Wait — was region pinning on for that tenant? I see fallback configured to override into the fallback region when probes fail.

priya: yes, fallback policy = regional-preference with override. We also have the geo-rewrite we shipped last week that rewrites region headers to us-west when probe latency > 150ms.

carol: That ring a bell — LB stickiness kept sessions but egress IPs changed -> flows landed on different NAT pools. SNAT exhaustion on us-west NAT gateway looks like the immediate cause.

luis: From logs: huge burst of long-lived inference connections (GPU tenant jobs) spilled into us-west after the rewrite. Those RPCs hold ephemeral ports for long periods.

nate: Can we flip Route53 weights or lower TTL to move traffic back quickly?

priya: TTL is 30s for our routing policy, but client-side caching + EDNS made endpoints stick. Also our fallback path used HTTP 302 redirects in some clients which keep the redirect for a while.

ops-bot: alert: NAT-ports remaining (us-west): 12, (ap-southeast): 340

carol: Short-term mitigation idea: add an egress-override at the LB for traffic class. Mark inference RPCs with `x-rw-class: heavy` and route them to a dedicated NAT pool (egress-gpu-1) instead of the shared pool. That isolates heavy flows.

luis: Example nginx map we can drop into the edge vhost to test quick (dev-only first):
```
map $http_x_rw_class $egress_pool {
  default "shared";
  "heavy" "egress-gpu-1";
}
proxy_set_header X-Egress-Pool $egress_pool;
```

nate: That sounds good but we have to be careful — rewriting egress pool touches routing metadata and metrics. Alternative immediate option: rate-limit long-lived RPCs after failover so ephemeral ports free up.

priya: Pragmatic plan: 1) adjust Route53 weights to 80/20 primary/fallback for ap-southeast->us-west (reduce spill), 2) add SNAT alarm threshold to get earlier notifications, 3) short-term LB rewrite pilot for heavy class, 4) long-term: dedicated egress pools + runbook update.

carol: I'll open a PR for the LB rewrite and test plan: simulate failover with 1k concurrent inference sessions in staging.

luis: Also propose adding a region_affinity cookie so clients stay pinned and avoid flip-flopping between regions during probe flaps.

nate: Assigning oncall to enact weight change now. Priya will monitor health metrics. I'll update infra playbook with the mitigation steps.

deploy-bot: route53-change applied by nate at 1865001500 — weights set to 80/20 for ap-southeast fallback group.

priya: After the weight change error rates dropped back to baseline. Leaving the LB rewrite PR and egress pool work as follow-ups. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

carol: filing retro + runbook update. Will ping infra docs owner for a follow-up.

priya: Retro tomorrow 09:00 PT to capture lessons and decide egress pool cadence.
